help.HOSTNAME: Optional. If MQTT is enabled, the topic name, object ID prefix, Home Assistant device name and ID are also set to this. See [MQTT](setup/software/mqtt/#enabling-mqtt).
help.DNS: Leave blank to use the gateway, which is correct on most home networks.
help.WIFICHANNEL: Force a specific channel. Set to 0 for autodetect.
help.WEBAUTH: Require HTTP Basic authentication for the web interface and OTA page. See [Web Server Authentication](setup/software/webserver_guide/#web-server-authentication).
help.HTTPPASS: Set a password before enabling password protection.
help.battery: The battery integration to use. Every supported battery has its own page with wiring and settings: see [Batteries](battery/).
help.CHGSTARQ: CHG_STA_RQ transmitted in 0x1F2. The LBC only acts on it while starting up, so a BMS reset is needed to apply a change. See [Nissan LEAF](battery/nissan_leaf_e_nv200/#software-configuration).
help.LEAFAUTOOFS: Each pack learns what its current sensor reads while its contactor is open, and subtracts that from the measured current. Needs contactor control.
help.INTERLOCKREQ: On a ZE0 (2011-2012 24kWh) battery, checks that the original high voltage connectors and SDS are properly seated before starting. On AZE0 and ZE1 batteries both HV plugs would have to be seated. See [Nissan LEAF](battery/nissan_leaf_e_nv200/#software-configuration).
help.DALYPWRPCT: Below 20% and above 80% SOC, limit power to this value * SOC% (e.g. 50 W/% means 150W at 3%, 500W at 10%). See [Daly BMS](battery/bms/daly_smartbms/#battery-emulator-configuration).
help.DALYDVSTART: Power limiting begins when pack voltage is this many dV above the discharge voltage limit (default 20 = 2.0V). See [Daly BMS](battery/bms/daly_smartbms/#battery-emulator-configuration).
help.DALYPWRDV: Max power per dV when approaching the discharge voltage limit. See [Daly BMS](battery/bms/daly_smartbms/#battery-emulator-configuration).
help.DALYPWRDEG: Max power added or removed per degree above or below 0°C. See [Daly BMS](battery/bms/daly_smartbms/#battery-emulator-configuration).
help.DALYPWR0C: Maximum allowed charge/discharge power at exactly 0°C. See [Daly BMS](battery/bms/daly_smartbms/#battery-emulator-configuration).
help.CHGPOWER: Continuous max charge power. Used since CAN data is not valid for this integration. Do not set too high!
help.DCHGPOWER: Continuous max discharge power. Used since CAN data is not valid for this integration. Do not set too high!
help.SOCESTIMATED: Switch to estimated State of Charge when accurate SOC data is not available from the battery.
help.CHGESTIMATED: Switch to estimated charge/discharge limits when accurate data is not available from the battery.
help.PYLONBAUD: CAN bus baudrate: 500kbps for most batteries, 250kbps for some configurations.
help.BATTPVMAX: Maximum safe voltage for the entire battery pack in volts. Used as charge target and protection limits.
help.BATTPVMIN: Minimum safe voltage for the entire battery pack in volts. Further discharge not possible below this limit.
help.BATTCVMAX: Maximum voltage per individual cell in millivolts. Charging stops if one cell reaches this voltage.
help.BATTCVMIN: Minimum voltage per individual cell in millivolts. Discharge stops if one cell drops to this voltage.
help.DBLBTR: Enable this option if you intend to run two batteries in parallel. See [Double battery](setup/software/battery_2x/).
help.TRIBTR: Enable this option if you intend to run three batteries in parallel. See [Triple battery](setup/software/battery_3x/).
help.inverter: The protocol the emulator speaks towards the inverter. Every supported inverter has its own page: see [Inverters](inverter/).
help.PYLONSEND: Select if we should send ###0 or ###1 CAN messages, useful for multi-battery setups or ID problems.
help.PYLONOFFSET: When enabled, 30k offset will be applied on some signals, useful for some inverters that see wrong data otherwise.
help.PYLONORDER: When enabled, byteorder will be inverted on some signals, useful for some inverters that see wrong data otherwise.
help.INVACCREB: When enabled, a non-zero RebootCommand written by the inverter to register 407 restarts the emulator, pausing charge/discharge and opening the contactors first. See [Fronius](inverter/fronius/#other-settings).
help.PRIMOGEN24: Use only in case you see 'Invalid battery size detected' message on Primo, with higher voltage batteries. See [Fronius](inverter/fronius/#invalid-battery-size-detected).
help.LOWPASSFILTER: Smooths sudden increases in the battery's charge power limits before sending them to the inverter to prevent oscillation, using a low pass filter. See [Inverter config](setup/software/webserver_guide/#inverter-config).
help.CHGTAPERSOC: Linearly reduces the allowed charge power from full power at the start SOC down to 0W at 100% scaled SOC, for a smooth approach to full instead of an abrupt cutoff. Mandatory and always enabled for some battery types. See [Inverter config](setup/software/webserver_guide/#inverter-config).
help.CHGTAPERSTART: Scaled SOC where charge power tapering begins. 95 = full power until 95%, then linear reduction reaching 0W at 100%. Limited to 50-85% for battery types where tapering is mandatory.
help.CHGTAPERFLOOR: Minimum charge power held during tapering until 100% scaled SOC is reached. Recommended to set it to 5-10% of the inverter's max power. 0 disables the floor, tapering goes linearly to 0W.
help.SLOWCANINV: Use a longer timeout for inverter still alive CAN messages.
help.INVOFFGRID: When enabled, faults that only mean the grid-tied inverter is absent are recorded as warnings instead, so they do not stop the battery from starting.
help.charger: An optional charger controlled by the emulator. See [Chargers](setup/chargers/).
help.CTOFFSET: Voltage offset required to calibrate 0A reading. -1 = auto-detect.
help.CTVNOM: Nominal voltage of the CT Clamp x10. Integer only.
help.CTANOM: Nominal current of the CT Clamp. Integer only.
help.CTINVERT: Invert the current reading from the CT clamp, +ve is charging, -ve is discharging.
help.EQSTOP: Type of the optional equipment stop button. Latching: a normally closed latching switch, the stop is active while it is pressed. Momentary: a normally closed push switch, a short press stops, holding it for 15 seconds resumes. See [Equipment stop](setup/software/equipment_stop/).
help.CNTCTRL: Let the emulator drive the contactors and the precharge through GPIO pins. See [Contactor control via GPIO](setup/software/contactor_control_via_gpio_pins/).
help.PRECHGMS: Time in milliseconds the precharge should be active. Set it to account for the resistance and capacitance of your inverter. See [Contactor control via GPIO](setup/software/contactor_control_via_gpio_pins/#software-setup).
help.NCCONTACTOR: Extremely rare option. If configured, GPIO control logic will be inverted for operation with normally closed contactors.
help.PWMCNTCTRL: Keeps the contactors engaged with a PWM signal to lower the power they draw. Requires solid state relays, test it properly with your contactors. See [PWM control](setup/software/contactor_control_via_gpio_pins/#pwm-control-for-lower-power-draw).
help.PWMFREQ: Frequency in Hz used for PWM.
help.PWMHOLD: 1-1023, lower value = lower power consumption. See [PWM control](setup/software/contactor_control_via_gpio_pins/#pwm-control-for-lower-power-draw).
help.PERBMSRESET: Power-cycles the BMS through a GPIO pin once every period. See [Periodic BMS reset](setup/hardware/periodic_bms_reset/).
help.PERBMSDEFSOC: Holds the reset back while either the real or the scaled SOC is below 15%. It runs as soon as SOC recovers, and the interval restarts from that point. See [Periodic BMS reset](setup/hardware/periodic_bms_reset/#local-trigger-on-battery-emulator).
help.PERBMSSKIPBAL: Gives up one occurrence if the battery reports balancing as active. The next occurrence runs even if balancing is still active. See [Periodic BMS reset](setup/hardware/periodic_bms_reset/#local-trigger-on-battery-emulator).
help.EXTPRECHARGE: Precharge the inverter side from an external high voltage source. See [External precharge](setup/hardware/high_voltage_source/).
help.MEASURECPUTEMP: If enabled, the CPU temperature will be displayed on the webserver.
help.CPUTEMPOFFSET: Unreliable CPU temperature readings can be corrected with an offset. Measure the actual temperature with a separate thermometer and adjust the offset accordingly.
help.ESPNOWENABLED: Send battery telemetry to nearby devices over ESP-NOW. See [ESP-NOW](setup/software/espnow/).
help.ESPNOWMACS: Comma separated list of receiver MAC addresses, e.g. AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF, 11:22:33:44:55:66 (max 8). Leave empty to broadcast to every device. Takes effect after a restart.
help.MQTTENABLED: Publish the battery data to an MQTT broker and accept commands from it. See [MQTT](setup/software/mqtt/#enabling-mqtt).
help.MQTTPUBLISHMS: How often to publish MQTT messages in seconds (1-300, step 1). Default: 5.
help.MQTTHEAP: Publish free heap, largest free block, minimum free heap and heap fragmentation to the /info topic and to Home Assistant autodiscovery. Takes effect after a restart.
help.REMBMSRESET: Act on the BMSRESET command topic (the Reset BMS button in Home Assistant). When disabled, the command is ignored. See [Periodic BMS reset](setup/hardware/periodic_bms_reset/#remote-trigger-through-mqtt).
help.HADISCEN: Publish Home Assistant MQTT discovery configs. The broker retains them, so Home Assistant keeps the entities without them being republished at every boot. See [Home Assistant Discovery](setup/software/mqtt/#home-assistant-discovery).
help.HADISCTOPIC: MQTT auto discovery base topic, homeassistant by default.
help.HADISCFWU: Publish the discovery configs once after every firmware update. They carry the software version and can gain or change entities between releases.
help.HADISC: Publish the discovery configs once after the next restart. Clears itself once they have been published.
help.PERFPROFILE: For developers. Get detailed performance metrics on the front page.
help.WEBENABLED: Enable this if you want general logging available in the Webserver. See [Log](setup/software/webserver_guide/#log).
help.USBENABLED: WARNING: Causes performance issues. Log general messages via USB cable. Avoid if possible! See [USB serial](setup/software/webserver_guide/#usb-serial).
help.CANLOGUSB: WARNING: Causes performance issues! Log incoming/outgoing CAN messages via USB cable. Avoid if possible! See [CAN logging](setup/can_related/can_logging/#usb).
help.SDLOGENABLED: Store logs on an SD card. Only works on hardware with SD-card slot. See [SD card](setup/software/webserver_guide/#sd-card).
help.CANLOGSD: Store incoming/outgoing CAN messages on SD card. Only works on hardware with SD-card slot. See [CAN logging](setup/can_related/can_logging/#sd-card).
help.SYSLOGEN: Send general logging as UDP syslog datagrams (RFC 5424) to a remote server. Events use their own severity; other lines are sent as debug. See [Remote syslog](setup/software/webserver_guide/#remote-syslog).
help.battwh: How much energy the battery can store. Some batteries report this over CAN; for the others set it manually, so that the inverter knows how large the battery is. See [Battery Capacity](setup/software/webserver_guide/#battery-capacity).
help.socscale: Extends battery life by rescaling the SOC within the configured minimum and maximum percentage, so the inverter never uses the whole battery. See [Rescale SOC%](setup/software/webserver_guide/#rescale-soc).
help.maxchga: Caps the current that can go into the battery. Set it to what your inverter, wiring or fuses allow, whichever is lowest (inverter power / minimum voltage). See [Battery charge/discharge limit](setup/software/webserver_guide/#battery-chargedischarge-limit).
help.maxdchga: Caps the current that can come out of the battery. Set it to what your inverter, wiring or fuses allow, whichever is lowest (inverter power / minimum voltage). See [Battery charge/discharge limit](setup/software/webserver_guide/#battery-chargedischarge-limit).
help.vlimits: Manually restrict charge/discharge to the target voltages below. If disabled, the emulator determines this based on the battery limits. Not all inverters support voltage based limits. See [Manual charge voltage limits](setup/software/webserver_guide/#manual-charge-voltage-limits).
help.bmsoff: How long the BMS power pin stays low during a periodic BMS reset. See [Periodic BMS reset](setup/hardware/periodic_bms_reset/).
help.recovery: Allows charging a severely undercharged battery at up to 5 A for 30 minutes. Recovering a too low cell can result in fire: keep the charge power low and watch the temperatures. See [Recovering an undercharged battery](setup/hardware/recovering_undercharged_battery/).
help.nocntctrl: This means you are either running CAN controlled contactors OR manually powering the contactors. Battery-Emulator will have limited amount of control over the contactors! See [Contactor control via GPIO](setup/software/contactor_control_via_gpio_pins/).
help.candump: CAN traffic will open in a new window. Let it run for the required amount of time and save the file. See [CAN logging](setup/can_related/can_logging/#webserver).
help.canreplay: Replays a CANdump .txt log (the format the CAN logging produces) onto the selected CAN interface, once or in a loop. See [CAN replay](setup/can_related/can_replay/).
